title: Minsky stage shows at St. Charles Theater, Tulane Stadium, trip to World's Fair
summary: Named bands played weekly at the St. Charles under Minsky; photos of Tulane Stadium and a 1933 road trip with Harry Burke.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Did you work any of the theaters with any other bands besides Forbes? Yeah, I worked at the, for Minsky, Harold Minsky, when they had a stage show. They didn't do too well with Burlesque or anything like that. So they put on, named bands would come in for a week and play at the St Charles Theater. St Charles Theater. That's right. It's torn down there. The International, Intercontinental. Intercontinental Hotel there. This is Ben Amaroff. I'm looking for that picture. Here's Gus Onry. You probably heard of him. And these were based in Louis and 33. This is Tulane Stadium. In God knows when. 1933. There's Tulane Stadium here. Just this side and that side. 22,000 people. Oh yeah, they did have wooden stands back here. After a while.

I thought that picture would be in here. This is when we went, Harry Burke and I went to the World's Fair in 33. This is Notre Dame University and this is, these are pictures taken along the road. Who was Harry Burke? Harry Burke was a piano player and an accordion player. More or less a teacher than he was a musician. This is for digging instruments, digging vibes and all. This is me. Really? Yeah, you don't recognize it.
Well you do look a little bit.
